sex.evidence: A total of 126 male Wistar rats (Rattus norvegicus)

dosing.doses_raw: 0.5, 1 and 2x the usual dose of 150 mL taken by a 70 kg person; A 1x dose corresponds to 0.514 mg/kg bw of DMT, 3.28 mg/kg bw of harmine, 0.793 mg/kg bw of harmaline, and 0.900 mg/kg of tetrahydroharmine
dosing.evidence: Gavage was used in the animals from the saline control group, fluoxetine positive group... and three ayahuasca treatment groups corresponding (adjusted to the animal bw) to 0.5, 1 and 2x the usual dose... Starting on day 2, the animals received their respective doses of Aya, fluoxetine, or DMT daily until day 14.

The DMT dose (1 mg/kg DMT resuspended in PBS) corresponded approximately to the level of DMT received by the Aya2 group... Starting on day 2, the animals received their respective doses of Aya, fluoxetine, or DMT daily until day 14.

group_housing.evidence: The animals were housed in polypropylene cages with galvanized wire tops, in ventilated racks from Alesco — cage density not stated

enrichment_housing.evidence: The animals did not receive any form of environmental enrichment to avoid interfering with the stress-induced depression model.

assays.assay_description: 5 min session in a circular white wooden arena (96 cm diameter, 34 cm height), floor divided into 18 squares with a central area. Measured: time in locomotion, number of crossing squares, entries into central area, rearing, grooming, defecation, urination.

application_type.evidence: Gavage was used for ayahuasca and fluoxetine groups; Animals received LPS and DMT by intraperitoneal (ip) injection

setup_restrain.evidence: Each animal was placed in the central area, and its behavior was observed for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: Open field apparatus; food/water not accessible during 5-min test

water_restriction.evidence: Open field apparatus; water not accessible during 5-min test

time_to_assay.evidence: The 126 animals included in this study underwent behavioral tests 24 h after the last treatment

sample_size.evidence: Each value represents the mean ± SEM of 16 to 18 animals

outcomes.summary: The Aya2 group showed increased total locomotion compared to fluoxetine and DMT groups, and Aya1 and Aya2 groups had significantly higher percentage of central entries than control. Rearing was higher in the Aya0.5 group. LPS alone did not significantly affect open field behavior versus control.
outcomes.statistics: p < 0.05, p < 0.01, p < 0.0001 (Kruskal-Wallis followed by Dunn's; one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey)
outcomes.evidence: Total locomotion in the open field arena... was significantly higher in the Aya2 group compared to the fluoxetine (p < 0.05) and DMT (p < 0.01) groups... the % of central entries relative to total locomotion was significantly higher (p < 0.01) in the Aya1 and Aya2 groups compared to control... Rearing behavior was higher in the Aya0.5 when compared to all other experimental groups

B1_num_measures.evidence: time in locomotion, number of crossing squares and entries into the central area, and frequency of rearing, grooming, defecation, and urination

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Each animal... was observed for 5 min and the following parameters were recorded (reported as totals)

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of transitions or behavioural sequences reported

B4_ethological.evidence: frequency of rearing, grooming, defecation, and urination

B5_social.evidence: Focal animal tested alone; no social construct

B6_cognitive.evidence: Open field assesses innate anxiety/locomotion, no learning component

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Trained observers quantified the predominant behavior; videos used to confirm observational data

E1_environment_type.evidence: circular white wooden arena, 96 cm in diameter and 34 cm in height

E3_bedding.evidence: Wooden floor divided into squares; no bedding mentioned

E6_spatial.evidence: Single circular arena with virtual zones (squares)

E7_social_context.evidence: Each animal was placed in the central area

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water accessible during the 5-min test

D1_continuity.evidence: On the 15th day, the animals underwent the open field... tests

D3_recording_days.evidence: On the 15th day, the animals underwent the open field... tests

D5_followup.evidence: Test was 24 h after last dose; no later follow-up performed

assays.assay_description: 5 min test in a transparent glass cylinder filled with water (23-25 °C) to a depth of 30 cm. Measured: swimming time, immobility time, climbing time, defecation. Behavior scored in 5-second intervals.

application_type.evidence: Ayahuasca and fluoxetine by gavage; DMT by i.p. injection

setup_restrain.evidence: forced swimming test was conducted in a transparent glass cylinder filled with water at 23 to 25 °C, to a depth of 30 cm (FST cylinder constitutes restraint per rubric)

water_restriction.evidence: Water is the test medium, not drinkable; no drinking water accessible during FST

time_to_assay.evidence: The 126 animals included in this study underwent behavioral tests 24 h after the last treatment

sample_size.evidence: Each value represents the mean ± SEM of 16 to 18 animals

outcomes.summary: Treatments with fluoxetine, ayahuasca, and DMT significantly increased swimming time compared to LPS group. DMT group had lower immobility than LPS. Fluoxetine and Aya0.5 groups showed higher climbing time compared to LPS and control.
outcomes.evidence: Animals from the LPS group spent significantly (p < 0.01) less time swimming than the ayahuasca and DMT groups... immobility was significantly (p < 0.05) higher compared to DMT... climbing behavior was lower in the LPS group, with significance (p < 0.01) when compared to fluoxetine and Aya0.5 groups

B1_num_measures.evidence: The time spent swimming, immobile, and climbing was recorded; defecation also reported

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Total times reported over the 5-min test; no within-session time-course analysis presented

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences reported

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility/swimming/climbing are not natural ethological behaviours per rubric

B6_cognitive.evidence: FST assesses behavioral despair, not learning or memory

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Trained observers quantified the predominant behavior in each 5-second interval

E1_environment_type.evidence: transparent glass cylinder filled with water

E3_bedding.evidence: Cylinder filled with water; no bedding

E8_food_water.evidence: Test water is not consumable; no food/water accessible

D1_continuity.evidence: Following the open field, the forced swimming test was conducted... for 5 min (single session)

D3_recording_days.evidence: On the 15th day, the animals underwent the open field and forced swimming tests

D5_followup.evidence: FST conducted 24 h post-last-dose only; no later follow-up

judge_notes: Two assays retained (OFT and FST) - all candidates agreed on these.
B1 for OFT: scored 3 (7+) because rubric explicitly counts locomotion time, square crossings, central entries, rearing, grooming, defecation, urination = 7 distinct measures.
B1 for FST: scored 2 (4-6) for swimming + immobility + climbing + defecation = 4 measures.
Ayahuasca schedule scored 'chronic' (13 daily doses, >7 days) per rubric definition; one candidate said 'repeated' but rubric specifies chronic = >=8 doses OR >7 days.
Setup restraint for FST scored 'yes' per rubric explicit listing of FST cylinder as restraint.
D5 followup scored 'no' for both assays: test at 24h post-last-dose is the primary test, no later post-acute recordings performed.
Group housing scored 'not_reported' - paper mentions polypropylene cages but does not state density.
Doses_mg_per_kg for Ayahuasca calculated from stated DMT content (0.514 mg/kg = 1x dose, so 0.5x ≈ 0.257, 2x ≈ 1.028).
